business_scope.primary_industry_name: Online Sales of Musical Instruments and Studio Audio Gear

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid: federal common-law framework combined with Quebec civil-law tradition; corporate constitution governed by the Business Corporations Act (Quebec), CQLR c. S-31.1, within Canada's federal statutory architecture
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: CETA (Canada-European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement)
CPTPP (Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership)
Canada-United States Tax Convention (1980, as amended) — double taxation agreement
OECD Multilateral Convention to Implement Tax Treaty Related Measures (MLI)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, S.C. 2000, c. 17, and its Regulations; Special Economic Measures Act, S.C. 1992, c. 17; United Nations Act, S.C. 1992, c. 20; Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act, S.C. 2017, c. 21; Criminal Code, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-46 (money-laundering and terrorist-financing offences); Business Corporations Act (Quebec), CQLR c. S-31.1 (register of individuals with significant control, added by Bill 68, assented to in 2022); Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c. P-44.1; Act respecting fighting against money laundering and terrorist financing activity, CQLR c. L-2.1 (enforced by the Autorité des marchés financiers)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Copy of passport or national identity card of every UBO and director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport or national identity authority of the UBO's country of citizenship
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized copy certified by a Quebec notary or commissioner for oaths; foreign-issued documents require a Hague Apostille (Convention entered into force for Canada on January 11, 2024) or, for non-Hague states, consular legalization by the relevant embassy or consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Sworn statutory declaration of ownership and control (declaration sous serment)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary of Quebec (Chambre des notaires du Quebec) or commissioner for taking oaths in Quebec
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Executed before a Quebec notary; if executed abroad, apostillized or consular-legalized prior to submission

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter or source-of-funds letter for each material UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for foreign-issued originals; Canadian bank letterhead documents are accepted directly by counsel without apostille

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing or equivalent compliance certificate for any corporate shareholder in the ownership chain
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent companies registry of the corporate shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if issued by a Hague member state; otherwise consular legalization at the foreign mission competent for Canada

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of every UBO, director, and authorized signatory against the Consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List (SEMA and UN Act), the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act (Magnitsky) list, the OFAC SDN List (bank and payment-processor requirement), and Quebec AMF AML/CFT directives. Domestic and foreign politically exposed persons, their family members and close associates trigger enhanced due diligence, source-of-funds and source-of-wealth verification, and senior-management approval under the PCMLTFA and its Regulations. All positive hits are escalated to counsel before incorporation; the complete screening record is retained for FINTRAC and AMF inspection.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec — online services portal (https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca); federal alternative for name grants: Corporations Canada Online Filing Centre (https://www.ic.gc.ca)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The official corporate name must be in French under the Charter of the French Language, CQLR c. C-11, and the Business Corporations Act (Quebec); the French name is the registered legal name and governs over any auxiliary version in another language. The name must contain an authorized legal element such as 'Inc.', 'Corp.', 'Ltee', 'Limitee', or 'Cie' (in French) or the English equivalents 'Incorporated', 'Corporation', 'Limited', 'Company' ('Ltd.', 'Corp.', 'Inc.', 'Co.') following the REQ acceptance rules. Transliteration of non-Latin script into the Latin alphabet is accepted for the French-prevalent name, provided the result does not create confusion with existing registered names or trademarks and is expressed using standard Canadian romanization.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: 'Bank' / 'Banque' — prior consent of the Bank of Canada or federal regulator required
'Insurance' / 'Assurance' — prior AMF licence or authorization required
'Stock Exchange' / 'Bourse' — prior securities regulator consent required
'Avocat', 'Notaire', 'Legal', 'Law' — prior bar or notary order consent required
'Quebec', 'Canada', 'Canadian' — prior ministerial consent and legitimate nexus required

Obscene, scandalous, or terrorizing expressions; false implications of government affiliation, public office, or regulated professional status; names of identifiable living persons without written consent

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Quebec), CQLR c S-31.1, ss. 9-30 (incorporation), s. 96 (directors' powers), ss. 406-410 (registered office); Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1, ss. 5-31 (registration and declarations). Federal alternative: Canada Business Corporations Act, RSC 1985, c C-44, ss. 8-19 (optional; requires extra-provincial registration in Quebec).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) — Quebec Enterprise Registry, Direction de l'immatriculation
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Statuts constitutifs) submitted through the REQ e-services portal as the 'Dépôt de statuts constitutifs'
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a Quebec business corporation. Shares may be issued for lawful consideration fixed by the board; no escrow, deposit, or capital contribution is required at incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the incorporators and initial directors, acting under the Business Corporations Act (Quebec), hereby: (1) accept the subscription for the initial common shares as recorded in the subscription register, authorize the allotment and issuance of share certificates, and direct that they be executed under corporate seal; (2) fix the registered office at the street address set out in the declaration of registration filed with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec; and (3) appoint [A] as President and Director and [B] as Secretary-Treasurer and Director, and authorize them to open bank accounts, file GST/HST and other registrations, and transact all ordinary business.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) — online 'Name Reservation Request' service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct an enterprise name search through the REQ search engine or a NUANS-style search; file the name reservation request online with up to three proposed name variants in French or bilingual form, including the legal element 'Inc.', 'Corp.', or 'Société par actions'. Hold the reserved name for the statutory period while articles are prepared.
required_dossiers: List of proposed corporate name variants
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused for confusing similarity, submit a fresh reservation with alternative variants within the same application or request a written REQ opinion; alternatively adopt a number name derived from the Quebec Enterprise Number (NEQ) plus the legal element.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Legal counsel (Barreau du Québec or Chambre des notaires du Québec) or REQ e-services
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the articles of incorporation setting out the corporate name, registered office address, share structure, director limits, and any share transfer restrictions. Have the incorporators execute the statuts constitutifs; notarization may be required for paper filings while REQ's secure electronic signature option can be used online.
required_dossiers: Identity and residence documents of incorporators
Registered office coordinates (street address, email, telephone)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct any formal deficiency noted by legal review or REQ and re-sign the defective page; an explanatory letter or amended draft may be submitted with the filing to cure omissions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Filing of Articles and Payment of Fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) — 'Deposit of Articles of Incorporation' electronic transaction
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the executed and notarized or electronically signed articles through REQ e-services, pay the incorporation duty of approximately CAD 335 by credit card or pre-authorized debit, and download the electronic Certificate of Incorporation containing the Quebec Enterprise Number (NEQ). The corporation comes into existence on the date of filing.
required_dossiers: Certificate of identity of directors or consent forms
Power of attorney if a third-party agent files
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If REQ issues a notice of query, respond in writing within the prescribed delay (typically 30 days) with corrections; if the deadline is missed, the remedy is to re-file after rectifying the articles and paying the fee again.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Resolution, Registered Office Declaration and Initial Corporate Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors and corporate secretary; Registraire des entreprises du Québec for the registered office declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene and adopt the first board resolution approving share subscriptions, fixing the registered office address, and appointing officers; file the initial declaration of registered office and director list with REQ within the statutory period; open the corporate minute book, issue share certificates, and adopt by-laws by resolution.
required_dossiers: Pro-forma first board resolution (the approved resolution text)
Initial declaration of registered office (REQ form)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct any omission by unanimous written resolution and file an amended or supplementary declaration with REQ; irregular minutes can be ratified by the directors at the next meeting.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration: CRA and Revenu Québec
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) — Business Registration Online; Revenu Québec — Business Number registration for QST/TVQ
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Enroll the corporation in the CRA Business Registration Online system to obtain the federal Business Number (BN); register for GST/HST (mandatory once gross revenue exceeds CAD 30,000) and for Quebec Sales Tax (QST/TVQ) with Revenu Québec under the same threshold; register as an employer and with CNESST for workplace coverage if staff are hired.
required_dossiers: NEQ number and legal name details
Bank account details for refunds and direct deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registration is rejected or incomplete, file an amendment request online or call the CRA business line to update BN program accounts; retroactive registration can be requested if the corporation was already carrying on business.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Occupancy Authorization and Workplace Clearance for Physical Premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local municipality urban planning and inspection department; municipal fire prevention service; Commission des normes, de l'équité, de la santé et de la sécurité du travail (CNESST)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Verify zoning compliance for online retail and warehousing in the chosen borough and apply for a municipal occupancy permit (certificat d'occupation) for the registered office and storage space. Arrange a fire safety inspection, disability access clearance, and compliance with the Quebec Building Code. Register the employer and workplace with CNESST if workers are present and post mandatory health and safety notices.
required_dossiers: Lease agreement or proof of ownership
Floor plans showing egress and storage areas
Fire alarm and extinguisher maintenance contracts
CNESST employer registration form and workplace poster
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Obtain inspection sign-off for minor deviations; apply for a minor variance or zoning exemption; if a stop-work order is issued, cure structural or fire deficiencies identified and request a reinspection before recommencing storage operations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs du Québec (MELCCFP) — Direction des autorisations industrielles (consultative only for this non-industrial retail activity)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Municipal Occupancy Permit (Certificat d'occupation) — no industrial manufacturing authorization or environmental certificate of authorization required for a pure online retail and distribution operation under the Environment Quality Act (CQLR c Q-2).

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs du Québec (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — no full environmental impact assessment and no registration required under the Regulation respecting environmental impact assessment (CQLR c Q-2, r. 23) because the activity is limited to warehousing, online sales, and distribution of musical instruments and audio gear; no listed industrial sector or new construction threshold applies.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial discharge of wastewater or VOCs is expected. Any HVAC refrigerant equipment must comply with the Regulation respecting halocarbons and Quebec's Clean Air Regulation (CQLR c Q-2, r. 15); packaging waste and e-waste (batteries and electronics) must be separated and traceably disposed of under the Residual Materials Management Regulation (CQLR c Q-2, r. 46). Municipal sewer discharge, if any, remains limited to sanitary volumes under the local sewer by-law; the Quebec discharge standard of 30 m³/day triggers a municipal permit only when exceeded.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the municipal fire prevention service confirming compliance with the Quebec Fire Safety Code for the warehouse and office; structural load inspection and occupancy certificate under the Quebec Building Code for the storage floor; CNESST occupational health and safety clearance covering signage, first-aid equipment, worker training and ergonomic handling of heavy instrument cases; municipal public protection clearance for egress and alarm systems.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA / Agence du revenu du Canada) for federal GST/HST and income tax; Revenu Québec for Quebec Sales Tax (QST) and provincial corporate tax. Portals: CRA My Business Account; Revenu Québec CLIC (Clic Revenu).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity carrying on business in Canada must register with CRA to obtain a Business Number (BN) and applicable program account (e.g., RC for GST/HST, RM for import/export, RP for payroll). Registration may be completed online through CRA's Business Registration Online, by mail, by fax, or through a representative. The entity must supply legal name, jurisdiction of incorporation, articles of incorporation/continuance, directors' information, Canadian contact/attorney for service, and expected revenue. For Quebec, separate registration with Revenu Québec is required to obtain a QST number (often integrated with the BN/QST registration through a coordinated form) when the entity carries on taxable commercial activity in Quebec.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not operate a check-the-box regime. Tax classification follows the legal form under corporate law. Specific elective provisions exist such as Income Tax Act s.85 (rollover of assets to a corporation) and s.216 (election for non-resident rental income to be taxed on a net basis). Anti-hybrid rules (ss. 18.2/18.4 and 57.1, 956–958) constrain deduction/non-inclusion mismatches and do not offer entity-classification elections.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax) plus QST (Quebec Sales Tax)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 in taxable supplies per single calendar quarter or over four consecutive calendar quarters; non-residents carrying on business in Canada are required to register once taxable supplies exceed this threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or mandatory API clearance regime is currently in force federally or in Quebec. CRA and Revenu Québec require invoices to contain the supplier's business number / QST registration number and to be retained as electronic records. Revenu Québec has announced a future mandatory e-invoicing framework, but it is not yet operative.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating under GST/HST and QST applies to supplies of goods that are exported from Canada, or supplied to a non-resident for use exclusively outside Canada, and to services supplied to non-residents where the place of supply is outside Canada and the service is not supplied in connection with Canadian real estate or goods. The supplier must obtain and retain evidence of export/foreign supply within prescribed timelines (normally immediately or as soon as practical).
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Québec may reassess within four years from the date of assessment, or ten years in cases of misrepresentation/negligence. False or fraudulent export zero-rating claims are subject to penalties of the greater of CAD 250 and 25% of the net tax amount, plus fines and interest. Criminal prosecution is possible for willful evasion, and improperly claimed credits may be clawed back retroactively with interest.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada), with the Department of Finance acting as the statutory authority for exchange control measures under the Currency Act and the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre (FINTRAC) responsible for transaction-level AML surveillance
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains full convertibility on both capital and current accounts under IMF Article VIII, with a freely floating exchange rate and no prior approval requirements for cross-border capital flows. Profit remittance and dividend distribution are subject to withholding taxes under Part XIII of the Income Tax Act (generally 25%, reduced to 15% under the Canada-US tax treaty, subject to applicable limitations) and to standard anti-money laundering transaction reporting under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender or conversion obligations apply to export proceeds in Canada. Exporters may hold, convert, or allocate foreign-currency accounts freely. Reporting obligations apply only for wire transfers crossing CAD 10,000 and tax filing requirements for worldwide income.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium. Payment-centric EMIs such as Stripe and PayPal are viable as front-end collection and payment gateways for consumer transactions in musical instruments and audio gear. They must register as Money Services Businesses in Canada under the PCMLTFA and comply with FINTRAC reporting. However, they are not OSFI-regulated deposit-taking institutions, cannot provide treasury services such as corporate credit facilities, foreign-exchange hedging, or multi-currency liquidity pools, and should not be used as the primary corporate treasury account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote account opening is technically permitted through FINTRAC-compliant digital identity verification methods. In practice, Tier 1 Canadian banks require a physical or video interview for foreign-controlled entities, and, where all directors are non-resident, the bank typically mandates an in-person attestation at a local branch or a level-2 notarised verification through a recognised legal representative. For a Quebec-registered entity, the Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) provides certified extracts and corporate records that materially reduce the documentary friction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque beneficial ownership structure involving non-resident shareholders or multi-tier holding companies
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: REQ corporate extract, federal Certificate of Existence, complete shareholder register, ultimate beneficial owner declaration with passport copies, formal organisational chart showing direct and indirect interest, and a written explanation of the capital source.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High cross-border wire volumes or transfers to perceived high-risk trading jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sales contracts, commercial invoices, bills of lading, customs entries, supplier agreements, end-customer order confirmations, and a documented trade rationale supported by a completed KYC questionnaire and annual financial projections.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Economic capital injection is performed via SWIFT MT103 with a precise purpose field: 'EQUITY CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION – CA_CORP – NEQ [9-digit Quebec Registration Number]'. The receiving institution must obtain a corporate resolution, any applicable pre-emptive rights waiver, and an updated Quebec registry extract. If the inbound transfer exceeds CAD 100,000, the bank may request source-of-wealth evidence including remitter bank statements, the share subscription agreement, and a valuation memo. No foreign-exchange conversion is mandated; funds may be booked as CAD or foreign-currency balance based on the account structure.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements to overseas manufacturers and suppliers are cleared through SWIFT MT103 with gpi tracking for direct transfers. For high-value documentary transactions, irrevocable commercial Letters of Credit (LC) are issued by the Canadian bank, entailing post-shipment documentation and negotiation with the foreign advising bank. CAD-denominated supplier payments to domestic partners are cleared through the Large Value Transfer System (LVTS) for same-day high-value settlement, and USD payments are cleared via Fedwire/CHIPS. Customer-facing collections are aggregated through Stripe and PayPal rails with settlement to the primary operational account.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Over-the-Counter Foreign Exchange Options (bilateral and prime-brokerage wrapper)

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal Annual Return (Canada Business Corporations Act)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada / Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary date of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing subject to CAD 100 late fee; continued delinquency leads to dissolution or administrative strike-off under CBCA

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days of the annual meeting or, if no meeting, within 6 months after the fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing subject to late fees (up to CAD 135); continued failure leads to administrative dissolution and removal from the register

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit only for distributing corporations or upon shareholder request (federal: 5% shareholding request; Quebec: any shareholder request). Private corporations can waive audit by unanimous shareholder resolution.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS (CPA Canada Handbook Part I) for publicly accountable enterprises; Canadian ASPE (Part II) for private corporations

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annual confirmation of significant control information is required in the Quebec Annual Declaration and, for federal corporations, in the Register of Individuals with Significant Control. Share transfer updates must be recorded in the Register of Members and, where applicable, the ISC register within 15 days.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control

stage_6.line_or_box_code: Page 1 – Box A (Legal Name / Trade Name)
stage_6.entry_description: The registered legal name and any operating trade name of the Canadian business corporation in Quebec
stage_6.non_resident_entry_guidance: State the exact name in the federal/Quebec charter; non-resident beneficial owners need not be listed; if there is a Quebec 'NEQ' registration, reconcile with Revenu Québec records.
